spec_points.description: Distinguish between scalar and vector quantities with examples
Add and subtract vectors by scale drawing and by calculation
Resolve a vector into perpendicular components
Define displacement, instantaneous speed/velocity, average speed/velocity, acceleration
Use SUVAT equations for uniform acceleration
Analyse motion from displacement-time and velocity-time graphs
Solve projectile motion problems using components
State and apply Newton's three laws of motion
Define momentum p = mv; state and apply Newton's 2nd law as F = Δp/Δt
Apply conservation of momentum to collisions and explosions
Define electric current as rate of flow of charge: I = ΔQ/Δt
Define potential difference V = W/Q and electromotive force
Explain current in terms of electron drift velocity: I = nAve
Define resistance R = V/I and state Ohm's law
Know and use R = ρL/A; define resistivity
Recall and use P = IV = I²R = V²/R
Describe the effect of temperature on resistance of metals and NTC thermistors
Calculate total resistance in series and parallel combinations
Apply Kirchhoff's laws to simple circuit analysis
Analyse potential divider circuits
Define tensile stress, tensile strain, and Young modulus
Describe the behaviour of materials under stress: elastic, plastic, fracture
Interpret and sketch stress-strain graphs for metals, polymers, and ceramics
Calculate energy stored in a stretched material: E = ½Fe = ½kx²
Describe longitudinal and transverse waves; identify crests, troughs, wavelength, frequency, period, amplitude
Use v = fλ
Describe reflection, refraction, and diffraction of waves
Apply the principle of superposition to construct resultant waves
Explain path difference and conditions for constructive/destructive interference
Analyse Young's double-slit experiment: λ = ax/D
Describe standing waves and explain nodes and antinodes
Apply Snell's law: n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂
Define refractive index n = c/v
Calculate the critical angle and explain total internal reflection
Explain the principles of optical fibres
Explain the photoelectric effect and its significance for the quantum model
Use E = hf and the equation hf = φ + ½mvmax²
Define threshold frequency and work function; explain why wave model fails
Describe wave-particle duality; use de Broglie wavelength λ = h/mv
Explain line emission and absorption spectra in terms of energy level transitions
Use ΔE = hf for photon emission/absorption
Understand the electronvolt as a unit of energy
Plan experiments to test hypotheses, including identification of variables
Identify systematic and random errors; understand accuracy and precision
Estimate and combine uncertainties using absolute and percentage methods
Present data in tables with appropriate significant figures; draw and interpret graphs
Define radian; use ω = Δθ/Δt, v = rω, a = v²/r = rω²
Apply F = mv²/r and identify centripetal force in context
Solve problems involving banking, conical pendulum, and vertical circles
State the defining condition for SHM: a = -ω²x; use x = A cos(ωt)
Use v = ±ω√(A²-x²); understand KE-PE interchange in SHM
Derive T = 2π√(l/g) for a simple pendulum and T = 2π√(m/k) for a mass-spring system
Define electric field strength E = F/Q; draw field line diagrams
Apply Coulomb's law F = kQ₁Q₂/r²
Know E = kQ/r² for a point charge; E = V/d for a uniform field
Define electric potential; use W = QV
Describe magnetic field patterns around wires and solenoids
Apply F = BIL sinθ and F = BQv sinθ
Explain and apply electromagnetic induction; use Faraday's and Lenz's laws
Understand and use transformers: Vs/Vp = Ns/Np
Describe the composition of the nucleus; define nucleon number, proton number
Describe properties of α, β, γ radiation and their interactions with matter
Write balanced nuclear equations for decay
Explain nuclear stability in terms of N-Z graph
Describe the quark model; identify up, down, strange quarks and their properties
Classify particles as hadrons (baryons, mesons) and leptons
Understand lepton number and baryon number conservation
State and use Boyle's law, Charles' law, and the pressure law
Use the ideal gas equation pV = nRT and pV = NkT
Derive and use pV = ⅓Nm<c²>; relate kinetic energy to temperature
Distinguish between internal energy, heat, and work
Define activity A = -dN/dt = λN; state units (Bq)
Use N = N₀e^(-λt) and A = A₀e^(-λt)
Define and calculate half-life: T½ = ln2/λ
Apply radioactive decay to carbon dating and medical tracers
Describe the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram and stellar evolution
Understand luminosity, flux, and the inverse square law
Use Wien's displacement law λmax ∝ 1/T and Stefan-Boltzmann law L = 4πr²σT⁴
Explain the Big Bang theory and evidence from red shift and CMB
State Hubble's law v = H₀d; estimate the age of the universe
Explain red shift and use Δλ/λ = v/c
Understand the evidence for dark matter and dark energy
Plan investigations to test relationships, controlling variables
Evaluate experimental methods and suggest improvements
Carry out detailed error analysis including propagation of uncertainties
